plan.contextChunk: This figure is a perspective line drawing of a rectangular coil rotating in a uniform magnetic field. The coil appears as a tall rectangular loop of several stacked turns, rendered as a striped gray band so the windings show, and tilted so its face is seen obliquely. A vertical axis labeled z passes through the coil's center, solid above and below the loop and dashed where it crosses the interior; a small circular arrow curls around its top to give the sense of rotation. A second axis labeled x runs diagonally toward the lower left, with a dashed segment continuing to the upper right. From the center point, a bold blue arrow labeled B points horizontally to the right as the uniform field, while an orange arrow labeled n-hat, the unit normal to the coil's surface, springs from the same origin and tilts down and to the right; a thin arc between the two marks the angle theta. Anchoring n-hat and B at a shared origin makes the angle between them the one quantity the reader tracks as the loop turns. The arrangement sets up the flux through a rotating coil and the emf that rotation induces.

elements: tall rectangular coil loop drawn as a striped gray band of several stacked turns (multi-turn winding), face seen obliquely
vertical z-axis line through the coil center, solid above and below the loop, dashed where it passes behind/through the loop interior
'z' label at top of vertical axis
small circular arrow curling around the top of the z-axis indicating rotation sense
diagonal x-axis running to lower-left with arrowhead, plus dashed continuation to upper-right through the loop
'x' label at lower-left end of the diagonal axis
short horizontal y-axis segment extending to the left of the origin
origin point at the center of the coil where all vectors are anchored
bold blue arrow pointing horizontally to the right from the origin, labeled 'B' with vector overbar
orange arrow from the origin tilting down and to the right, the unit normal, labeled 'n̂'
thin arc between the blue B arrow and the orange n̂ arrow with 'θ' label
flux/emf readout text (Φ = BA cos θ, ε = NBAω sin θ)
graph panel (alternate view): synchronized Φ(t) and ε(t) sinusoidal traces with time axis and moving playhead marker

interactions.teaches: Only the component of B along the coil normal contributes to flux: as θ grows the orange n̂ swings away from B and the flux readout falls as cos θ, vanishing when the coil face is edge-on to the field.
interactions.label: Coil angle θ (degrees)

interactions.teaches: Steady rotation makes θ increase linearly in time, so the flux varies sinusoidally and the induced emf — its rate of change — is largest exactly when the flux passes through zero.
interactions.label: Rotate coil at constant ω

interactions.teaches: Links the geometric angle between n̂ and B in the 3D picture to the sinusoidal Φ(t) and ε(t) curves used in the AC-generator calculation.
interactions.label: View

interactions.teaches: Confirms that n̂ is genuinely perpendicular to the coil plane and that both n̂ and B lie in the horizontal plane while the rotation axis stays vertical.

demo_steps.title: Face-on: maximum flux
demo_steps.narration: At θ = 0 the orange normal n̂ points straight along B, the coil face is broadside to the field, and the flux reaches its maximum BA.

demo_steps.title: Tilted coil
demo_steps.narration: Drag θ to 35°: only the component of B along n̂ threads the loop, so the flux drops to BA cos 35°.

demo_steps.title: Edge-on: zero flux
demo_steps.narration: At θ = 90° n̂ is perpendicular to B, field lines skim past the coil plane and the flux is zero — yet this is where the flux is changing fastest.

demo_steps.title: Read the curves
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the graph view: Φ traces BA cos θ while ε traces NBAω sin θ, a quarter cycle out of step.

demo_steps.title: Continuous rotation
demo_steps.narration: Play the steady spin with both panels shown — the turning angle between n̂ and B is what generates the alternating emf.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: coil loop is a rectangle 2.0 wide × 3.0 tall (outer), drawn as a flat band of thickness 0.10 with 4–5 visible stacked turns (stripes offset ~0.03 along the coil normal), band width 0.10. Coil is centered on the origin and pivots about the vertical z-axis; at θ = 0 the coil plane contains z and the x-axis (plane normal along +y). Axes: z vertical from -3.2 to +3.4 (solid outside |z|>1.5, dashed inside the loop interior), label 'z' at top; x-axis runs toward the viewer's lower-left from origin to length 3.2 with arrowhead and 'x' label, and continues as a dashed ray to the upper-right for 2.2 units; y-axis shown only as a short solid horizontal segment 1.2 units to the LEFT of the origin (screen-left). Rotation arrow: small ellipse of radius 0.45 around the z-axis at z ≈ 2.6 with an arrowhead giving the spin sense. B vector: bold blue arrow from origin along +y (screen-right), length 2.2, shaft thickness ~0.07, label '𝐁' with overbar at its tip. n̂ vector: orange arrow from the origin, length 1.3, lying in the horizontal xy-plane but drawn in this view as tilting down and to the right; direction n̂ = (−sin θ·x̂ + cos θ·ŷ) so θ is measured from B. Theta arc: thin black arc of radius 0.55 spanning from the B direction to n̂, with 'θ' label just outside its midpoint. Colors: coil band gray #9E9E9E with lighter #C9C9C9 highlight stripes and thin dark outlines #555; axes and labels black #000; B arrow blue #1F6FD0; n̂ arrow and its label orange #F07C1E. Physics: Φ = B·A·cos θ with A = 2.0 × 3.0 (use B = 1 T, A = 1 m², N = 1 for readouts unless labeled otherwise); ε = N·B·A·ω·sin θ with θ = ωt, ω default such that one revolution ≈ 6 s. Graph view: two stacked plots over two full periods, Φ (blue) as cosine, ε (orange) as sine, shared time axis, vertical playhead line tied to the current θ.
interactionPlan.notes: Use PerspectiveCamera (fov ~35) with OrbitControls, target at the origin. Build the multi-turn coil from 4–5 concentric extruded rectangle outlines (THREE.Shape with a hole, or TubeGeometry along a rounded-rectangle path) grouped and offset along the local normal, then rotate the whole group about the world Y (up = z) axis by θ so the coil, n̂, and the theta arc stay rigidly linked. Dashed axis segments via LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances(). Vectors as ArrowHelper or custom cylinder+cone meshes so the blue B arrow can be drawn noticeably thicker. Theta arc as a Line built from a small arc of points in the horizontal plane, regenerated each frame. Labels (z, x, B, n̂, θ, flux readout) as CSS2DRenderer/sprite overlays so they stay screen-facing and legible. Graph view rendered in a 2D canvas or SVG overlay panel driven by the same θ state; in 'Both' mode dock it to the right third of the frame and shrink the 3D viewport rather than moving the camera. Animation drives θ with a clock delta and simply writes back into the slider value so slider and animation share one state variable.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for coil angle theta: the learner drags the loop around the z-axis, the orange n-hat vector sweeps relative to the blue B vector and a flux readout follows BA cos(theta), showing that only the field component through the coil area contributes to magnetic flux.
- Animation for steady rotation: the learner plays the rotating coil, the loop spins while flux and induced emf traces update together, making clear that alternating emf comes from the time-changing angle between n-hat and B.
- Toggle between vector view and graph view: the learner switches from the 3D coil diagram to synchronized flux/emf curves, connecting the geometric angle in the picture to the sinusoidal quantities used in the calculation.

authoredContext:
A Rectangular Coil Rotating in a Magnetic Field A rectangular coil of area A and N turns is placed in a uniform magnetic field B→=Bj^, as shown in the figure. The coil is rotated about the z-axis through its center at a constant angular velocity ω. Obtain an expression for the induced emf in the coil.

A rectangular coil rotating in a uniform magnetic field.

Figure shows a rectangular coil rotating in a uniform magnetic field.

Strategy According to the diagram, the angle between the perpendicular to the surface (n^) and the magnetic field (B→) is θ. The dot product of B→·n^ simplifies to only the cosθ component of the magnetic field, namely where the magnetic field projects onto the unit area vector n^. The magnitude of the magnetic field and the area of the loop are fixed over time, which makes the integration simplify quickly. The induced emf is written out using Faraday’s law.

discrepancies: Initial camera/orientation is wrong: the coil is rendered almost edge-on (a thin dark slab) whereas the source clearly shows the broad rectangular coil face as a large parallelogram — the most recognizable feature of the figure is lost.
The B vector reads as a slanted down-right arrow instead of the horizontal right-pointing arrow of the source, and n̂ is foreshortened almost onto B, so the θ angle between them is barely visible.

The coil's multi-turn gray frame with an open window (5 stacked windings, light/dark banding, white interior) is not readable at this angle — it looks like an opaque solid slab rather than the layered wire frame of the source.
All 3D labels (z, x, B, n̂, θ) are rendered very small relative to the canvas, far less prominent than the bold serif annotations in the source; the θ label in particular is almost invisible.
Extra bottom readout strip (θ · Φ · ε) and the graph-overlay panel are additions not in the source figure (acceptable pedagogically, but they change the composition).
Overall figure occupies a small fraction of the viewport, so the coil, axes and vectors are much smaller relative to the frame than in the source.

demo_steps.title: Face-on: maximum flux
demo_steps.narration: At θ = 0 the orange normal n̂ points straight along B, the coil face is broadside to the field, and the flux reaches its maximum BA.

demo_steps.title: Tilted coil
demo_steps.narration: Drag θ to 35°: only the component of B along n̂ threads the loop, so the flux drops to BA cos 35°.

demo_steps.title: Edge-on: zero flux
demo_steps.narration: At θ = 90° n̂ is perpendicular to B, field lines skim past the coil plane and the flux is zero — yet this is where the flux is changing fastest.

demo_steps.title: Read the curves
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the graph view: Φ traces BA cos θ while ε traces NBAω sin θ, a quarter cycle out of step.

demo_steps.title: Continuous rotation
demo_steps.narration: Play the steady spin with both panels shown — the turning angle between n̂ and B is what generates the alternating emf.
